Q24910792.summary: On the lid of this small reliquary for a fragment of the True Cross, Christ stands on the cross in a long purple colobium, his eyes open, flanked by the Virgin and Saint John, with busts of saints set in green enamel around the border and along the sides. Its bright emerald, blue and maroon enamel is simple, even naive, in execution, yet full of life. Made around the time of the struggle over images, it presents the crucified Christ as alive and victorious.
facts: The Greek inscriptions on the lid include Christ's words 'Here is your son ... Here is your mother'; under the lid, niello scenes show the Annunciation, Nativity, Crucifixion and Anastasis.
Inside, walls in the shape of a patriarchal (double) cross divide the box into compartments, the main one probably for a relic of the True Cross.
Dates proposed range from about 815 to 843, around the second phase of Byzantine Iconoclasm; The Met gives 'early 9th century' (accession 17.190.715a, b, gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1917).
Q24910792.notes: Place of manufacture is debated; Constantinople is most often proposed, but Wikipedia also discusses Rome as a possible source of the enamel craft.

cur:manuscripts-kells-temptation-of-chri.summary: Christ appears from the waist up on the pinnacle of the Temple, drawn as a great patterned roof, holding a scroll; at his left a small black, winged figure of Satan tempts him, while two angels hover above. A crowd of heads fills the left side, and within the Temple a small half-figure appears in a doorway, with more people gathered below. It illustrates the moment in Luke when the devil sets Christ on the pinnacle of the Temple.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the crowd to Christ's right may represent his disciples; the figure in the Temple doorway has been variously interpreted.
The facing page (fol. 203r) begins 'Iesus autem plenus Spiritu Sancto' (Luke 4:1), the opening of the Temptation narrative, in a fully decorated text page.

cur:manuscripts-khludov-ascension.summary: In the margin beside the text of Psalm 46, Christ sits enthroned and blessing within an oval mandorla carried up by four angels; below, on a hilltop among olive trees, the Virgin stands in a dark mantle among the apostles, who gaze and gesture upward. The image interprets the psalm verse 'God is gone up with a shout' as a prophecy of Christ's Ascension.
facts: The Khludov Psalter is a 'marginal psalter': the outer edges of its pages were left blank to be filled with pictures, linked to particular verses by small arrows.
It is one of only three illuminated Byzantine psalters to survive from the 9th century, a generation after the end of Iconoclasm.
cur:manuscripts-khludov-ascension.notes: Folio not recorded on the Commons file (photographed from a reprint). The psalm number ΜΖ (46, Septuagint numbering) is visible beside the miniature.
